items.title: Deferred aggregate families admit identity-free values
items.statement: Each deferred aggregate family requires only schema_version while its key-defining identifiers are optional. Before owner-specific schemas exist, a value can validate without the project, artifact, thread, provider, account, lane, or checkpoint identity needed to prove that it belongs under its key. Deferral prevents present implementation authority, but the registry supplies no executable rejection oracle for premature writers.
items.impact: Premature or generic writers can persist structurally valid but unjoinable records, and consumers cannot distinguish corruption from an intentionally sparse projection.
items.builder_discretion: Owner schemas should bind every key component into the value or state an explicit key-only identity rule, then provide rejection fixtures before implementation authority is granted.

items.title: Provider identity is labeled non-blocking despite an open launch-currentness blocker
items.statement: The provider runtime identity family is marked deferred_not_build_blocking, yet its own replay rule says discovery/currentness must be proved before launch and its deferred reason says the provider stream blocker remains open. No freshness timestamp, expiry, verification state, or discovery generation is listed, leaving both readiness classification and stale-identity rejection ambiguous.
items.impact: A readiness consumer can treat the family as harmlessly deferred while routing or usage attribution relies on stale or unverified identity at launch.
items.builder_discretion: Separate build-blocking from launch-blocking status and define an executable freshness/currentness record plus its rejecting consumers.

evidence.exact_quote: "replay_behavior": "Deferred; provider stream readiness must prove discovery/currentness before launch.",

items.title: Terminal hierarchy has no referential-integrity or membership invariants
items.statement: Workspace, section, and tab schemas type their ordering and active-reference fields but do not require uniqueness, membership, existence, same-project ownership, or reciprocal parent-child consistency. A workspace may name missing or duplicate sections, a section may activate a tab outside its order, and a tab may point at an unrelated pane root.
items.impact: Partial writes, compaction, or untrusted imports can produce valid records that restore a broken hierarchy or misleading active selection in the GUI.
items.builder_discretion: Define atomic hierarchy update semantics and validate uniqueness, membership, existence, project scope, and reciprocal links on write and recovery.

items.title: Pane records do not enforce a valid acyclic split tree
items.statement: pane_kind is not coupled to parent, children, split_axis, or size_fraction. The schema permits a leaf with children and a split axis, a split with no children, cycles, multiple parents, cross-tab children, negative or greater-than-one size fractions, and multiple roots.
items.impact: Restoration can loop, drop panes, mis-size layout, cross-link tabs, or crash on a record set that passes per-row schema validation.
items.builder_discretion: Add kind-dependent constraints, bounded fractions, and a graph-level oracle for one rooted acyclic same-project same-tab tree with exactly one parent for non-roots.

items.title: Persisted active session references have no explicit stale state
items.statement: The prose correctly says restored state is historical and process liveness must be revalidated, but active_terminal_session_id and terminal_session_id are bare ids with no last-validated time, liveness state, relaunch disposition, or validation generation. The value contract does not tell GUI consumers how to represent the interval before revalidation or a failed revalidation.
items.impact: A restored tab or leaf can appear live or active even when the process is gone, and failure/relaunch transitions cannot be rendered from persisted truth.
items.builder_discretion: Persist or derive an explicit unknown/stale/revalidating/dead/relaunched state and require the GUI to avoid a live affordance until runtime validation succeeds.

evidence.exact_quote: "replay_behavior": "Restores tab metadata and pane-tree root for historical layout review only.",
"replay_behavior": "Restores the leaf pane's last known session reference for history; runtime must revalidate or relaunch any process separately.",

items.title: Concurrent layout updates lack a write-conflict contract
items.statement: The workspace schema has an optional layout_generation and timestamps, but no required revision, compare-and-swap token, writer identity, monotonicity rule, merge policy, or idempotency key. Child rows have timestamps only. Concurrent GUI/editor projectors can therefore overwrite ordering or active selection without a detectable conflict.
items.impact: Rapid split, close, move, and selection operations can lose updates or leave parent and child records from different generations.
items.builder_discretion: Require a generation or revision on every hierarchy mutation and define transaction/CAS boundaries, retry behavior, and generation-coherent reads.

items.title: Compaction prose has no deletion state, cascade order, or rollback behavior
items.statement: Retention rules depend on references expiring, but materialized schemas have no tombstone, deleted_at, compaction generation, pending-delete state, or recovery marker. The order for deleting workspace, section, tab, pane, leaf, session, command-block, and workgroup references is unspecified, as is rollback after a partial transaction.
items.impact: A crash or partial compaction can create dangling records or permanently discard layout/history still reachable from another family.
items.builder_discretion: Define transactional cascade/tombstone semantics, orphan quarantine, retry idempotency, and a post-compaction integrity oracle.

items.title: Migration contracts omit atomicity, idempotency, and malformed-input handling
items.statement: The migration statements name record splitting/import goals but do not define source-version detection, duplicate resolution, stable id mapping, interruption resume, rollback, quarantine, or post-migration validation. The pane and leaf split is especially vulnerable to cross-record partial success.
items.impact: A restart or malformed legacy blob can duplicate rows, lose hierarchy edges, or leave mixed old/new state with no deterministic repair path.
items.builder_discretion: Specify a versioned migration state machine with stable identity mapping, transactional batches, resumable checkpoints, quarantine, rollback, and invariant tests.

items.title: Ref-only and no-secret rules are not enforceable from the value schemas
items.statement: cwd_ref, shell_profile_ref, titles, and descriptions are unrestricted strings. Nothing distinguishes an opaque safe reference from a raw path, control sequence, credential, command fragment, or secret-bearing environment value. redaction_profile is declarative metadata and does not prove that the other strings were scrubbed.
items.impact: Untrusted imports or buggy producers can persist sensitive material and inject terminal control or misleading display text while the row still claims no_secrets.
items.builder_discretion: Define opaque-ref formats and trusted resolvers; bound and sanitize user-visible strings; make redaction provenance/verdict independently verifiable rather than self-asserted.

evidence.exact_quote: "redaction_no_secret_rule": "cwd and shell profile are refs only; raw paths with secrets, env values, and output buffers are forbidden.",

items.title: All hierarchy collections and display strings are unbounded
items.statement: section_order, terminal_tab_order, child_pane_ids, and workspace_tab_ids have neither maxItems nor uniqueItems; titles and descriptions have no size bound. Canonical messagepack does not by itself cap decoded allocations or graph traversal.
items.impact: A malformed or adversarial row can cause excessive storage, allocation, rendering, traversal, or quadratic integrity-check cost.
items.builder_discretion: Set product-backed limits for hierarchy breadth/depth, workgroup membership, and text bytes/code points, with decode-before-allocation guards and rejection fixtures.

items.title: Cross-project references are schema-valid and lack an authority check
items.statement: Keys include project_id, but referenced workspace, section, tab, pane, session, command-block, cwd, shell-profile, and resource-budget ids are generic strings. The contracts do not require referenced objects to belong to the same project or to an authorized visibility domain.
items.impact: A forged or corrupted value can splice another project's layout or sensitive reference into the current project, causing disclosure or destructive cross-project cleanup.
items.builder_discretion: Enforce project-scoped typed ids or a resolver authorization check on every reference and include cross-project rejection tests.

items.title: Recovery, liveness validation, migration, and compaction consumers are unnamed
items.statement: The materialized terminal families name terminal GUI and Runtime Artifacts panel as consumers, while replay, migration, retention, and liveness prose requires runtime validators, restore coordinators, migration runners, and compactors. No such caller/consumer ownership or failure contract is identified in this window.
items.impact: Critical lifecycle behavior can remain unimplemented or be inconsistently duplicated because the value family has no named operational consumer accountable for it.
items.builder_discretion: Name each lifecycle consumer and its read/write authority, transaction boundary, error surface, and acceptance oracle.

evidence.exact_quote: "replay_behavior": "Restores terminal workspace layout and selected ids as historical GUI state only; replay never certifies terminal process liveness.",

items.title: User-visible ordering and labels lack localization and accessibility semantics
items.statement: The schemas store raw section, tab, leaf, and workgroup titles plus visual ordering, but do not carry a stable accessible name, label provenance, locale/normalization contract, directionality handling, or distinction between user-authored and generated labels. Empty strings are valid for all title fields.
items.impact: Restored GUI groupings can be unnamed to assistive technology, sort inconsistently across normalization forms, or display generated labels in the wrong language/direction.
items.builder_discretion: Define whether labels are user-authored or localization keys, apply Unicode normalization and bidi-safe display rules, and provide accessible-name fallback and empty-label tests.

items.title: Corruption and repair observability is unspecified
items.statement: The value rows contain updated timestamps and redaction profiles but no integrity verdict, repair provenance, last validated generation, corrupt/quarantined state, writer identity, or diagnostic reference. This window also provides no behavior for decode failure or graph-level invariant failure, so operator-visible recovery and support evidence remain unknown.
items.impact: Support tooling cannot distinguish stale, corrupt, partially migrated, unauthorized, or merely missing terminal state, nor prove what automated repair changed.
items.builder_discretion: Define corruption classification, quarantine and repair receipts, validation generation, diagnostic redaction, and operator-facing oracles.

items.title: Replay text explicitly refuses to infer process liveness
items.statement: The workspace, section, pane, and leaf replay rules consistently describe restored layout as historical and require runtime validation or relaunch instead of treating persisted references as proof of a live process. That negative constraint is explicit and materially reduces false-authority risk, although G-005 identifies the missing representational state around revalidation.

evidence.exact_quote: "replay_behavior": "Restores terminal workspace layout and selected ids as historical GUI state only; replay never certifies terminal process liveness.",
"replay_behavior": "Restores split tree layout; leaf liveness remains runtime-validated and is never inferred from this value.",

items.title: Materialized row schemas are closed and version-bound
items.statement: Each shown materialized terminal value schema rejects undeclared properties and binds schema_id and schema_version to constants. This is a concrete compatibility and untrusted-input strength at the single-row shape layer, distinct from the cross-row gaps above.

items.title: Persisted terminal layout has no declared network dependency
items.statement: The materialized terminal state families use local redb storage and their replay behavior concerns local historical GUI state. Within this window, network loss is not a prerequisite for decoding or restoring the stored layout; provider/network readiness is isolated in a deferred family.

dimension_assessments.summary: Operational consumers for restore, liveness validation, migration, compaction, and repair are not named.
Per-row schemas permit identity-free deferred values, inconsistent hierarchy membership, and invalid pane graphs.
No required revision or coherent transaction generation protects multi-row layout changes.
Multi-row hierarchy writes, migrations, and compaction lack partial-success and resume semantics.
No rollback, quarantine, repair, or idempotent resume contract accompanies migration or destructive cleanup.
Generic reference ids can cross project boundaries and provider readiness classification is internally ambiguous.
Secret-free/ref-only assertions are not enforced and deletion lifecycle has no tombstone or cascade contract.
Closed schemas are a non-gap, but unrestricted strings and graph references still admit hostile content and topology.
Historical active ids have no explicit stale/revalidating/dead state, and broken membership can misstate active GUI selection.
Materialized terminal layout is local redb state with no declared network prerequisite in this window; provider readiness is separately deferred.
Collections, graph breadth/depth, and display strings are unbounded.
Persisted user-visible group labels can be empty and have no accessible-name fallback or semantic provenance.
Label locale, generated-versus-user-authored semantics, normalization, and bidirectional display handling are unspecified.
Version constants are explicit, but legacy split/import behavior lacks a deterministic resumable migration protocol.
Corruption, quarantine, repair, validation generation, and writer provenance are not represented.
Compaction rules do not define tombstones, safe cascade order, crash recovery, or post-delete integrity checks.
Deferred owner schemas and operational consumers are unresolved seams; provider status conflicts with its launch-currentness rule.
The window lacks executable rejection or recovery oracles for graph integrity, cross-project refs, migrations, compaction, stale liveness, and size limits.
Decode-failure, corruption classification, repair provenance, and malformed legacy-state behavior are absent, leaving residual operational behavior unknowable from this window.
